verdict.rationale: Consensus's own docs say its REST API and MCP server "expose the same retrieval and synthesis surface that powers the web app": search, paper detail, synthesis and the Consensus Meter, plus filter parameters such as excludePreprints. That parity claim is limited to retrieval and synthesis. UI features like Library import (Zotero/BibTeX/RIS), Citation Graph, Threads, Deep Search and account management have no documented API equivalent, and the advertised OpenAPI spec link is dead while docs.consensus.app is walled, so the full API surface cannot be verified. Missing for 10: documented API coverage of library/reference management, citation graph, threads and deep search, a reachable machine-readable API contract, and independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: API and agent ready: a REST API and an MCP server expose the same retrieval and synthesis surface that powers the web app
search, paper detail, synthesis, and the Consensus Meter as stable, versioned JSON endpoints with bearer-token authentication
pass `exclude_preprints=true` (MCP) or `excludePreprints=true` (REST API) to filter to peer-reviewed papers only.
